question.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by $L(x)=(Ax-2b)^{T}(Ax-2b)$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{x}L(x)$ at $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
We can solve this problem by applying the chain rule for gradients.

Let $y=Ax-2b.$ Then, $L(x)={y}^{T}y,$ and

$$
{∇}_{x}L={(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}x})}^{T}={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{T}\cdot {(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}y})}^{T}.
$$

Now, since 

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{T}y)=2{y}^{T}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(Ax-2b)=A,
$$

we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}L & ={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{T}\cdot {(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}y})}^{T} \\  & ={A}^{T}\cdot 2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}L & ={A}^{T}\cdot 2y \\  & =2\cdot {A}^{T}(Ax-2b) \\  & =2\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}([\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]-2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =2\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}58 \\ 26\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
